s1.syndrome_frame: Pelvic mass with chronic abdominal pain and vaginal discharge
salient_findings: Pelvic mass extending to two fingers below the umbilicus
key_facts: 48-year-old postmenopausal woman
Gravida 2, para 2
3-month history of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge
Fluctuating lower abdominal pain
Fever
Progressive abdominal enlargement over 15 years
Difficulty with defecation and voiding
Previous attempted myomectomy with severe adhesions
Elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level of 115.6 g/dL
Smooth, firm pelvic mass on rectovaginal examination
Limited mobility of the pelvic mass
Cervix could not be visualized or sondaged
Transabdominal ultrasound showed a hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity
Separate homogeneous solid mass in the left adnexa
Abdominal and pelvic computed tomography demonstrated a multilocular cystic mass

shortlist.label: Uterine fibroid with cystic degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Pelvic mass with cystic degeneration and previous myomectomy attempt

shortlist.label: Infected hematometra
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level, brown-yellowish vaginal discharge, and hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity

shortlist.label: Degenerating fibroid
shortlist.why_kept: Smooth, firm pelvic mass and history of progressive abdominal enlargement

shortlist.label: Ovarian fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Separate homogeneous solid mass in the left adnexa and multilocular cystic mass on CT

shortlist.label: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level and uterine cavity distended with fluid and air

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge, fluctuating lower abdominal pain, fever, and progressive abdominal enlargement, combined with the ultrasound and CT findings of a hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity and a distended uterine cavity with fluid and air, are most consistent with infected hematometra.

rejected.label: Uterine fibroid with cystic degeneration
rejected.why: While possible, the presence of fever and fluctuating pain suggests an infectious component, which is not typical for uterine fibroids with cystic degeneration alone.

rejected.label: Degenerating fibroid
rejected.why: Degenerating fibroids can cause pain and degenerative changes, but the presence of fever, discharge, and an air-fluid level within the uterine cavity points more towards an infectious process.

rejected.label: Ovarian fibroma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and imaging findings do not specifically suggest an ovarian origin for the patient's symptoms, and the presence of a mass within the uterine cavity is not consistent with an ovarian fibroma.

rejected.label: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: While the elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level could suggest malignancy, the combination of symptoms and imaging findings, particularly the presence of an air-fluid level within the uterine cavity, is more indicative of an infectious process than a malignant one.
